Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
3	# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
4	#
5	# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
6	#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
7	#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
8	#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
12	#
13	# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
14	# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
15	# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
16	set -uo pipefail
17	
18	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
19	
20	DRY_RUN=0
21	PHASES=()
22	for arg in "$@"; do
23	  case "$arg" in
24	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
25	    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
26	    *)
27	      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
28	      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
29	      exit 2
30	      ;;
31	  esac
32	done
33	[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)
34	
35	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
37	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
38	
39	pass=0
40	failed=0
41	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
42	
43	# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
44	run_case() {
45	  local name="$1"; shift
46	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
47	  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
48	  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
49	  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
50	    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
51	  else
52	    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
53	    cat "$log"
54	  fi
55	  rm -f "$log"
56	}
57	
58	run_unit() {
59	  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
60	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
61	    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
62	    return
63	  fi
64	  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
65	    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
66	  fi
67	  shopt -s nullglob
68	  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
69	  shopt -u nullglob
70	  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
71	    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
72	  fi
73	  local t
74	  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
75	}
76	
77	run_contract() {
78	  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
79	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
80	    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)" \
81	      "tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh (each)"
82	    return
83	  fi
84	  local s
85	  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh \
86	           "$ROOT"/tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh; do
87	    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
88	    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
89	  done
90	}
91	
92	run_e2e() {
93	  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
94	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
95	  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
96	}
97	
98	for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
99	  case "$p" in
100	    unit)     run_unit ;;
101	    contract) run_contract ;;
102	    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
103	  esac
104	done
105	
106	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
107	  echo
108	  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
109	  exit 0
110	fi
111	
112	echo
113	step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
114	if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
115	  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
116	  exit 1
117	fi
118

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# B2 lint: tests/e2e.sh must detach stdin (`</dev/null`) from every
3	# interactive-by-default subprocess it spawns (QEMU `-nographic`, vsim under
4	# `timeout`). Without it, a backgrounded shell group (scripts/run_e2e.sh uses
5	# one) lets SIGTTOU stop the child when it calls tcsetattr on the inherited
6	# controlling tty. Diagnostic tell: empty log + rc=124 + /proc/$PID/status
7	# State `T`. See memory `feedback_qemu_timeout_sigttou`.
8	#
9	# This is a static lint: it greps the QEMU1 and vsim invocation blocks in
10	# tests/e2e.sh for the `</dev/null` redirect. Catches accidental removal of
11	# the SIGTTOU workaround without needing a real QEMU/vsim build.
12	
13	set -uo pipefail
14	
15	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
16	E2E="$SCRIPT_DIR/e2e.sh"
17	
18	fail() { echo "FAIL[e2e_stdin_detached]: $1"; exit 1; }
19	
20	[ -r "$E2E" ] || fail "cannot read $E2E"
21	
22	# Block 1: QEMU 1 spawn (no `timeout`, but `-nographic` + tty-inherited stdin
23	# is still SIGTTOU-prone under backgrounded shell groups).
24	qemu1_block=$(awk '/QEMU 1: drain entry state/,/^QEMU1_RC=/' "$E2E")
25	[ -n "$qemu1_block" ] || fail "QEMU 1 block not located"
26	echo "$qemu1_block" | grep -q '</dev/null' \
27	  || fail "QEMU 1 invocation missing </dev/null"
28	
29	# Block 2: vsim spawn -- wrapped by `timeout`, which forks a new process
30	# group. tcsetattr on the inherited tty triggers SIGTTOU; the kernel stops
31	# the process and `timeout` eventually SIGKILLs at TIMEOUT.
32	vsim_block=$(awk '/vsim: resume \+ drain/,/^VSIM_RC=/' "$E2E")
33	[ -n "$vsim_block" ] || fail "vsim block not located"
34	echo "$vsim_block" | grep -q '</dev/null' \
35	  || fail "vsim invocation missing </dev/null"
36	
37	echo "[e2e_stdin_detached] PASS"
38

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# B3 lint: scripts/run_e2e.sh must anchor FILTER regex matches.
3	#
4	# The bash conditional `[[ "$name" =~ $FILTER ]]` does substring matching
5	# by default. With FILTER=rt_csr, the user expects a single fixture but
6	# rt_csr / rt_csr_survival both match (and any future rt_csr_*). To run
7	# multiple fixtures, the user can pass an explicit regex (e.g.
8	# FILTER='rt_csr.*'). The default policy is exact match.
9	#
10	# This static lint greps each FILTER comparison and requires the regex
11	# to be wrapped with `^` and `$`. Catches accidental removal of the
12	# anchors without needing a real test run.
13	
14	set -uo pipefail
15	
16	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
17	RUN_E2E="$SCRIPT_DIR/../scripts/run_e2e.sh"
18	
19	fail() { echo "FAIL[run_e2e_filter_anchored]: $1"; exit 1; }
20	
21	[ -r "$RUN_E2E" ] || fail "cannot read $RUN_E2E"
22	
23	# Every `=~ ... $FILTER ...` should be of the form `=~ ^$FILTER$`.
24	matches=$(grep -nE '=~ +\^?\$FILTER\$?' "$RUN_E2E" || true)
25	[ -n "$matches" ] || fail "no FILTER regex sites found"
26	
27	while IFS= read -r line; do
28	  if ! echo "$line" | grep -qE '=~ +\^\$FILTER\$'; then
29	    fail "unanchored FILTER regex at: $line"
30	  fi
31	done <<< "$matches"
32	
33	echo "[run_e2e_filter_anchored] PASS"
34

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# RED->GREEN: resolve_pc maps an ROI boundary (a symbol name OR a 0x-hex
3	# address) to a bare hex address, resolving symbols against `nm` output.
4	# This is the primitive that lets pc mode point at ANY symbol/address
5	# instead of the planted _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc markers.
6	set -uo pipefail
7	
8	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
9	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/roi.sh"
10	
11	fail() { echo "FAIL[roi_resolve]: $1"; exit 1; }
12	
13	# Fake `nm --defined-only` output (columns: addr type name).
14	NM_FIXTURE='0000000000100002 T _hybrid_enter_pc
15	0000000000100020 T _hybrid_exit_pc
16	0000000000100040 T vmatmul_kernel
17	0000000000100000 T main'
18	
19	# 1. hex passthrough strips the 0x prefix, keeps the digits.
20	got=$(resolve_pc "0x100abc" "$NM_FIXTURE")
21	[ "$got" = "100abc" ] || fail "hex passthrough: want 100abc got '$got'"
22	
23	# 2. uppercase 0X prefix also stripped.
24	got=$(resolve_pc "0X1f" "$NM_FIXTURE")
25	[ "$got" = "1f" ] || fail "0X prefix: want 1f got '$got'"
26	
27	# 3. arbitrary symbol name resolves via nm output.
28	got=$(resolve_pc "vmatmul_kernel" "$NM_FIXTURE")
29	[ "$got" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "symbol resolve: want ...100040 got '$got'"
30	
31	# 4. unknown symbol -> empty (caller turns this into a FAIL).
32	got=$(resolve_pc "nope" "$NM_FIXTURE")
33	[ -z "$got" ] || fail "unknown symbol: want empty got '$got'"
34	
35	# --- roi_resolve_pair: env-required + dual resolve, as e2e.sh uses it ---
36	
37	# 5. unset ROI_START/ROI_END -> error (no implicit fallback).
38	unset ROI_START ROI_END
39	out=$(roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t 2>&1)
40	[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "unset pair: expected nonzero return"
41	case "$out" in *"ROI_START and ROI_END"*) ;; *) fail "unset pair: missing required-vars message: '$out'";; esac
42	
43	# 6. ROI_START symbol + ROI_END hex resolve to ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC.
44	ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END=0x100100 roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t \
45	  || fail "override pair: returned nonzero"
46	[ "$ENTER_PC" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "ENTER_PC: got '$ENTER_PC'"
47	[ "$EXIT_PC"  = "100100" ]            || fail "EXIT_PC: got '$EXIT_PC'"
48	
49	# 7. an unresolvable boundary fails loudly and names the offender.
50	out=$(ROI_START=ghost ROI_END=main roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" myfix 2>&1)
51	[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "bad start: expected nonzero return"
52	case "$out" in *"myfix"*"ghost"*) ;; *) fail "bad start: message missing label/symbol: '$out'";; esac
53

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
3	#
4	# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
5	# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
6	# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
7	# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
8	# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.
9	
10	# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
11	#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
12	#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
13	# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
14	# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
15	resolve_pc() {
16	  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
17	  case "$boundary" in
18	    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
19	    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
20	  esac
21	}
22	
23	# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
24	#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (both REQUIRED), resolves
25	#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
26	#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
27	#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
28	roi_resolve_pair() {
29	  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
30	  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
31	  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
32	  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
33	    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
34	    return 1
35	  fi
36	  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
37	  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
38	  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
39	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
40	    return 1
41	  fi
42	  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
43	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
44	    return 1
45	  fi
46	  return 0
47	}
48	
49	# roi_markers_from_disasm <objdump_disasm>
50	#   Derives the two pc-mode switch PCs from the ROI marker HINTs a fixture
51	#   embeds, scanning `objdump -d` text:
52	#     ENTER = the entry marker     `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`  (encoding 5a002013)
53	#     EXIT  = the LAST exit marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`  (encoding 5a102013)
54	#   Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
55	#   (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
56	#   (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC reproduces
57	#   marker mode's switch points exactly -- no offset arithmetic here. EXIT
58	#   keeps the LAST marker so a fixture that jumps over poison exit-marker
59	#   padding (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first
60	#   dead one. The raw-bytes match is mnemonic-independent, so no objdump
61	#   decode table is needed.
62	#   Prints "ENTER EXIT" as bare hex; returns 1 (prints nothing) if either
63	#   marker is absent. This lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no
64	#   per-fixture config; ./andesim run still passes explicit boundaries.
65	roi_markers_from_disasm() {
66	  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
67	    $2 == "5a002013" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
68	    $2 == "5a102013"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }
69	    END {
70	      if (enter != "" && exit_pc != "") { print enter, exit_pc }
71	      else                              { exit 1 }
72	    }
73	  '
74	}
